audit.why: TRICKY at 7.5/10 fits a 54.05% win rate over 692 games: Mordekaiser owns levels 2-3 and 6, Poppy owns both item rows.
audit.corrected: Difficulty left at 7.5/10, matching the mirror's read that the lane swings to Poppy from first item onward.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Poppy, Skill, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser in both layers — five rows disagree with the packet and with the whys printed beside them.
audit.why: whys[0] says level 1 is neutral, whys[3] says 4-5 is even, whys[5] and whys[6] both say Poppy holds the favour. The sides contradicted their own explanations and the 692-game packet.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3, 5 and 6 flipped as one atomic paired group in both layers: Skill, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, Skill, Mordekaiser, Poppy, Poppy — identical to the packet and the mirror. Ratings moved with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Multiple fields claim Steadfast Presence (W) stops or grounds Death's Grasp, and one claims Mordekaiser has a dash. Death's Grasp is a pull on the target, not a dash by Mordekaiser, and Mordekaiser has no dash at all.
audit.why: Poppy's W only stops dashes; telling the player to hold W as a parry against his E gets them pulled with W wasted for 12-20s. Mirror states the same from Mordekaiser's side.
audit.corrected: Dash-denial claims removed; W restated as the armour/MR steroid it actually is here, and the real interaction — Heroic Charge needs a wall, Realm of Death (650 range, 140/120/100s) removes the wall option by moving you — kept front and centre.

audit.whatIsWrong: Indestructible's heal is described but Grievous Wounds timing is never given, despite the item block already hinting at it.
audit.why: His shield converts stored damage into a heal; without anti-heal your flat Hammer Shock chunk is refunded every trade.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal timing added to the mid block.

edits.before: Passive shield trades + Q zone control win early. Identify how Mordekaiser contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: One ability each and low bases — level 1 is neutral. Deny his Obliterate last-hits and read which wall you would slam him into later.

edits.before: W deletes his dash mid-flight — hold it like a parry. Only take the trade when Mordekaiser's Realm of Death is down.
edits.after: Death's Grasp lands at 2 and drags you into an isolated Obliterate, which hits hardest on a single target — hold the wave back.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Mordekaiser must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: He pulls with Death's Grasp on 16s, stacks isolated Obliterate, and Indestructible heals it back. Fight only with a wall behind him.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Realm of Death's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Even window: your max-HP Hammer Shock chunk trades against his scaling Obliterate. Bank small leads, and start anti-heal against his shield heal.

edits.before: Keeper’s Verdict punts the fight’s biggest threat across the map. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Mordekaiser's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Realm of Death, 650 range on 140s, drags you somewhere with no friendly wall and steals your resists. Never sit low while it is up.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Realm of Death's cooldown.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet plus cheap resists absorbs isolated Obliterate — your kit is gold-independent, so this is your window.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Mordekaiser carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: You hold the side lane, where his R can only ever isolate you — the worst target for it. Close the map before his items outgrow your flat damage.

edits.after: E Mordekaiser into a wall while Death's Grasp is on its 16s cooldown, Q the zone under him, and leave before Indestructible converts to a heal.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are roughly even — your flat damage doesn't scale with points the way his Q does, so lean on Q's percent chunk and short E-stun resets rather than raw trades. Level 6 is HIS window, not yours: his Realm of Death (R) yanks you into a 1v1 and steals your armor/MR/AP scaling, and you're exactly the kind of tanky low-econ target it isolates cleanly. Don't be below ~60% when his ult is up, and save your own R for the kick-out or to bodyblock — it's peel and displacement here, not a kill button.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are roughly even — your flat damage doesn't scale the way Obliterate does, so lean on Q's percent chunk and E-stun resets, and buy Grievous Wounds early because Indestructible turns every stored trade into a heal. Level 6 is HIS window: Realm of Death (650 range, 140s) yanks you into a 1v1 with no wall to slam him into and steals your resists. Don't be below ~60% while it is up, and keep your own R for the kick-out — peel here, not a kill button.

edits.before: By first item you're comfortable — cheap tank components let you out-trade and survive his Q-isolation, and your W dash-deny plus E wall-stun stay valuable no matter your gold, so you hold the favor the 54% reflects. Keep this matchup a sidelane 1v1 where his R can only ever pull you, the worst possible target for it. In teamfights flip the script with W to ground his E engage onto your carry and E him off — you don't out-scale him into the hyper-late, so close out the map advantage before his items snowball his Q and shield past your flat damage.
edits.after: By first item you're comfortable — cheap tank components let you survive isolated Obliterate, and your E wall-stun stays valuable no matter your gold, so you hold the favor the 54% reflects. Keep this a sidelane 1v1 where his R can only ever pull you, the worst possible target for it. In teamfights his R is the threat to your carry, so stand between them and E him off the moment he lands it — you don't out-scale him, so close the map before his items push Obliterate and the shield past your flat damage.
